meta.note: Decision register. Every question that must be answered before a decision can reasonably be made, split by whether we already have the answer. 'Open - blocking' questions stop a decision until evidence arrives. 'Open - owner input' questions need a value only the owner can set; a proposed default is given so work is not stalled.
meta.rule: A value appears in the Answer column only if it was read from a linked official source. Otherwise the Answer column is blank and the row is flagged.

questions.q: What is the official closing line for each NFL game?
questions.known: The NFL itself publishes no betting lines or odds. Nothing on nfl.com exposes a price.
questions.missing: A licensed, timestamped odds feed including closing prices.
questions.evidence: Not available from any league-official source. The only league-authorised wholesale path for official NFL sports-betting data is Genius Sports (SRC-006).
questions.blocks: Every market-comparison, CLV and validation gate.

questions.q: Does an official NFL depth chart exist?
questions.known: The league publishes rosters and injury reports, not depth charts.
questions.missing: Nothing - the answer is established negatively.
questions.evidence: Direct fetch of https://www.nfl.com/teams/kansas-city-chiefs/depth-chart returned the NFL 404 page.
questions.blocks: REQ-010, REQ-011, REQ-012 until a snap-share substitute is built.

questions.q: What are the official injury-report categories?
questions.answer: Practice participation: Did Not Participate, Limited Participation, Full Participation. Game status: Out, Doubtful, Questionable.
questions.known: These are exactly the categories rendered on the official Week 10 report that we read in full.
questions.missing: The written policy text could not be located on an official domain. Two candidate URLs on operations.nfl.com and one on nfl.com returned 404.
questions.evidence: Categories observed directly across all 254 rows of the official report.

questions.q: What are the official definitions of Out / Doubtful / Questionable, and what are the filing deadlines?
questions.known: Widely reported as: Out = will not play; Doubtful = unlikely to play; Questionable = uncertain. Practice reports Wed/Thu/Fri, game status due Friday 4:00 PM ET, inactives 90 minutes before kickoff.
questions.missing: An official NFL page stating any of it. We attempted operations.nfl.com/gameday/nfl-game-status, operations.nfl.com/inside-football-ops/health-and-safety/injury-report and nfl.com/injuries/inactives - all returned HTTP 404.
questions.evidence: None official. Deliberately NOT asserted as fact on this site.
questions.blocks: Any model that maps a designation to a probability.

questions.q: How large is the book's structural edge (vig / hold) that a strategy must beat?
questions.answer: Nevada statewide sports pool hold: 7.72% for the reported month, 6.06% fiscal-year-to-date (Nevada Gaming Control Board, May 2025 Gaming Revenue Report).
questions.known: An official government regulator publishes realised hold.
questions.missing: Hold is Nevada-specific and not NFL-specific; it is a proxy, not an NFL number.
questions.evidence: Official NGCB revenue report table, sports pool line: win $41,158 thousand (month) at 7.72% hold; $449,816 thousand fiscal-year-to-date at 6.06% hold.

questions.q: Is the NFL betting market efficient at the close?
questions.known: The published literature is genuinely mixed: several studies find closing lines broadly efficient, others find exploitable exceptions in specific subsets (large spreads, high totals, specific bias patterns).
questions.missing: A single authoritative verdict does not exist. We have not run our own test.
questions.evidence: Academic literature on NFL and MLB line movement, reviewed but not independently reproduced this session. No value is asserted.
questions.blocks: Choice of CLV as the primary skill metric (it is chosen anyway, because it is the only metric that does not require waiting for results).

questions.q: How many bets are needed before a strategy can be called skilful rather than lucky?
questions.answer: Sample size is a function of the edge and the odds, not a fixed number. The register specifies the calculation rather than asserting a number.
questions.known: The calculation is standard: for a binomial record at price p, the number of bets n needed to detect edge e at 95% confidence scales with p(1-p)/e-squared. Because e is small, n is large - typically in the low thousands at standard -110 prices.
questions.missing: The realised edge of any of our strategies, which is unknown until backtested.
questions.evidence: Statistical methodology, not an empirical claim. No NFL-specific number is asserted.

questions.q: Are player-prop correlations published anywhere officially?
questions.known: No league-official or regulator-official source publishes a prop correlation matrix. Sportsbooks price same-game parlays with proprietary, undisclosed correlation models.
questions.missing: Either a licensed correlation feed, or enough historical joint data to estimate correlations ourselves.
questions.evidence: Not found. Every value in the correlation register is therefore left blank - see F-010.
questions.blocks: Honest pricing of parlays and player-prop combos (REQ-005).

questions.q: What is the bankroll, and what staking rule should be used?
questions.known: Nothing. The brief does not state a bankroll.
questions.missing: A bankroll figure and a risk tolerance.
questions.proposed_default: Fractional Kelly at one-quarter of full Kelly, capped at 1% of bankroll per position, until the owner sets otherwise.
questions.evidence: None required - this is a preference, not a fact.
questions.blocks: Position sizing. Does not block signal research.

questions.q: Which sportsbooks and which jurisdiction?
questions.known: Nothing. The brief does not name a market or jurisdiction.
questions.missing: Jurisdiction, licensed operators, and whether real money is ever staked or the leaderboard is paper-traded only.
questions.proposed_default: Run the leaderboard on paper (no real stakes) until a jurisdiction and licensed operator are confirmed.
questions.evidence: None required.
questions.blocks: Live deployment only. Does not block research.

questions.q: Is a historical odds archive available?
questions.known: The official injury report has a season selector running back to 1965, so a multi-decade official injury archive exists. No equivalent official odds archive exists.
questions.missing: Timestamped historical prices, both opening and closing, for a large sample of games and props.
questions.evidence: Injury archive confirmed present on the official page; odds archive not found on any official source.
questions.blocks: Backtesting, and therefore every validation gate.

questions.q: What are the actual correlation values between the props we want to combine?
questions.known: The sign (positive or negative) of several relationships is a structural consequence of how football works, but the magnitude is not known to us.
questions.missing: Historical joint outcomes for every prop pair we intend to combine.
questions.evidence: None. Deliberately left blank.

questions.q: What reward structure should the leaderboard use?
questions.known: Nothing.
questions.missing: Whether rewards are monetary, reputational or internal.
questions.proposed_default: Score on risk-adjusted skill metrics (CLV and calibration), not raw profit, with a minimum-bets floor so a lucky short run cannot win.
questions.evidence: None required.

questions.q: How are strategies submitted, versioned and frozen?
questions.known: Nothing.
questions.missing: A submission convention.
questions.proposed_default: One strategy per registered file, immutable version identifier, declared in-sample window, mandatory untouched holdout window, and a declaration signed before the holdout is scored.
questions.evidence: None required.

questions.q: Is official player-tracking (Next Gen Stats) data available to us?
questions.known: Next Gen Stats is official NFL data and is distributed exclusively by Genius Sports through the 2027-28 season.
questions.missing: Whether we hold or can obtain a licence, and how much history the licence covers.
questions.evidence: Partnership terms read from the issuer's own announcement.

questions.q: What is the official weather source for outdoor games?
questions.known: NOAA / the National Weather Service is the official US government source and is the obvious candidate.
questions.missing: Nothing blocking - but no weather value has been ingested, so no weather value appears anywhere on this site.
questions.evidence: Not read this session.

questions.q: Which teams are on bye in Week 10?
questions.known: DEN, PHI, CHI and TB do not appear on the official Week 10 injury report, and the official standings show all four with exactly 9 games played while all 16 teams appearing on the report that have 8 games played are playing this week.
questions.missing: Direct confirmation from the official schedule, which was not read this session.
questions.evidence: Cross-check of two official sources; the conclusion is an arithmetic inference, not a read value. Flagged F-008.

questions.q: Which club is at home in each Week 10 matchup?
questions.known: The official injury report lists two clubs per matchup without an explicit home/away label in the retrieved markup.
questions.missing: The official schedule.
questions.evidence: None. Deliberately not asserted. Flagged F-009.

questions.q: Which players are on IR, PUP or NFI and therefore invisible on the injury report?
questions.known: A player moved to IR leaves the injury report entirely. This is demonstrated directly: the Seahawks show 'No Injuries Reported' on the official Week 10 report while NFL.com news simultaneously reports QB Sam Darnold ruled out for that game.
questions.missing: The official transactions feed.
questions.evidence: Official injury report plus official NFL.com news headline, read together. Flagged F-004.
questions.blocks: REQ-009 - injury tracking is materially incomplete without it.

questions.q: How should 'skill' be defined for the leaderboard?
questions.answer: Skill is defined as the ability to beat the closing line after costs, persistently, out of sample. Profit alone is explicitly rejected as a skill measure because it is not separable from variance.
questions.known: This is a definition we set, not an empirical finding.
questions.missing: Nothing.
questions.evidence: Definition, stated explicitly so it can be challenged.

questions.q: Do we have any historical play-by-play at all?
questions.known: The nflverse open-source project redistributes official NFL data and is a candidate convenience source, but it is a community mirror, not an official source.
questions.missing: A decision on whether Tier-3 community data is acceptable, and a re-verification pass if it is.
questions.evidence: Not read or used this session. No value on this site comes from it.

questions.q: What is the refresh cadence the system must support?
questions.answer: Ingest the official practice report on each of the three filing days, the game-status report when filed, and the inactive list after it is published; re-price immediately on each change.
questions.known: Cadence is dictated by when the official report changes, which we observed directly.
questions.missing: Automation. The current snapshot is a one-time manual-equivalent read.
questions.evidence: Observed structure of the official report.

questions.q: How much of the official injury report is usable as published?
questions.answer: 248 of 254 listed players have an empty Injuries (body part) column. Only 6 rows carry an injury description.
questions.known: Measured directly from the ingested report.
questions.missing: Body-part detail for 97.6% of listed players.
questions.evidence: Counted from the ingested official data. Flagged F-003.
questions.blocks: Any signal that keys off injury type.

questions.q: Is there a record of who decided what, and why?
questions.answer: Yes, from this session onward: the suggestion register carries a decision record per item and COORDINATION.md carries the session log.
questions.known: Governance artefact, not a data question.
questions.missing: Nothing.
questions.evidence: Repository artefacts.
